H&P – Super Detailed

Consult Summary:
45-year-old male with 3-day history of watery diarrhea (6–7×/day), intermittent left-lower abdominal cramping, initial vomiting, subjective fever, and loss of appetite—clinical picture most consistent with acute gastroenteritis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Watery, loose stools requiring frequent toilet visits for past 3 days.  
• Onset & course: Began 3 days ago; frequency stable at 6–7 bowel movements/day. Vomited on day 1 only; no current vomiting. Pain intermittent.  
• Character of pain: Cramp-like, left lower abdomen, comes and goes, non-radiating.  
• Associated symptoms: Weakness, shakiness, subjective fever at onset, loss of appetite.  
• Absent symptoms: No blood in stool or vomitus, no current fever, no night sweats.  
• Triggers/exposures: Ate Chinese takeaway 4 days ago; one child vomited but no similar diarrhea in household.  
• Diet/fluids: Tolerating fluids, taking soups/smoothies; maintains hydration.  
• Functional impact: Must stay near toilet; continues working as accountant with difficulty.  
• Review of systems: No chronic bowel disease, no other systemic complaints reported.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – well controlled with inhaler.  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.  
• Medications: Inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); no additional regular meds.  

Social History:
• Lives with wife and 2 children.  
• Employment: Accountant; has worked during illness.  
• Tobacco: Never smoker.  
• Alcohol: Denies use.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed during remote consultation (no vitals or exam findings documented).

Investigations:
• None to date. Stool studies planned if symptoms persist beyond 3–4 days.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected acute viral vs bacterial gastroenteritis
  – Advice: Conservative management.  
  – Hydration: Encourage oral fluids; recommend oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte) as needed.  
  – Antipyretic/analgesia: Paracetamol 2 tablets up to 4 ×/day for fever or pain.  
  – Diet: Light foods as tolerated.  
  – Work: Recommend 2–3 days off for rest and to reduce contagion.  
  – Red flags/Follow-up: Return if no improvement in 3–4 days, worsening symptoms, blood in stool, inability to maintain hydration. If persistent, arrange stool culture and further evaluation.

Issue 2: Risk of dehydration
  – Monitor fluid intake/urine output.  
  – Seek urgent care if signs of dehydration (dizziness, reduced urine, persistent vomiting).

Issue 3: Chronic asthma (stable)
  – Continue regular inhaler use; no changes required.

General plan items:
  – Provide sick note if needed for employer.  
  – Reinforce hand hygiene to reduce household spread.  

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: Drug allergies, full medication list with doses, vitals, physical examination findings.  
• Internal conflicts: Patient reports no current fever but did feel febrile 3–4 days ago (noted).  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational fillers, no significant omissions.
